title: 6.27.3 Sub-build: A checkered board
description: Two loops, one test with %, one rect per square: the light and dark board drawn from row and column numbers.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The canvas is empty. `draw()` takes the outline away with `noStroke()`, but nothing draws a square yet.

steps.title: Every square
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, write two loops, one inside the other: `for (let r = 0; r < N; r++)` and inside it `for (let c = 0; c < N; c++)`. Inside both, `fill('#ead9b6')` and draw `rect(c * CELL, r * CELL, CELL, CELL)`. Run: the canvas fills with 64 light squares that meet edge to edge, so it looks like one big square.
hints: `r` is the row and goes down the screen, so it sets y; `c` is the column and sets x.
Loop to `N`, not to 8, so the loops always match the board.

steps.title: Dark when odd
steps.instructions: Change the `fill` so it picks the colour: `fill((r + c) % 2 === 1 ? '#7a5a40' : '#ead9b6');`. Run: a checkered board, with a light square in the top-left corner.
hints: Square (0, 0) adds to 0, which is even: light. Square (0, 1) adds to 1: dark.
Try `=== 0` instead of `=== 1` and the colours swap.

requirements.title: Two loops, one inside the other
requirements.description: One loop visits the rows and a second loop inside it visits the columns. Help: 6.27.2 (Reading: A board is a grid of letters)
requirements.hint: for (let r = 0; r < N; r++) { for (let c = 0; c < N; c++) { ... } }

requirements.title: A test with % 2
requirements.description: The colour is picked by a test on the row plus the column with % 2. Help: 6.27.2 (Reading: A board is a grid of letters)

requirements.title: A square at each row and column
requirements.description: Each square is a rect placed from its column and row times the cell size. Help: 6.27.2 (Reading: A board is a grid of letters)
requirements.hint: rect(c * CELL, r * CELL, CELL, CELL);

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: A checkered board". The task: draw an 8 by 8 checkered board with two loops, one inside the other, picking a dark colour when the row plus the column is odd ((r + c) % 2 === 1, or another correct test) and drawing one rect per square from its column and row times the cell size. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries, nested ifs, switch statements and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.
